:::{#exm-block-inverse}
#### The bottom-right entry of the inverse of a $2 \times 2$ matrix

<!-- no-figure: one 2 x 2 inverse checked entry by entry; nothing to plot -->

Let $\matr{X} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$ with $\matr{A} = [5]$,
whose [Schur complement](#def-schur-complement) is $\matr{S} = [\tfrac{9}{5}]$ (@exm-schur-complement).
It is [positive definite](#def-positive-definite) (@exm-schur-test), so by @thm-block-inverse:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{T}
&= \matr{S}^{-1} \\
&= [\tfrac{5}{9}].
\end{aligned}
$$

Directly, $\matr{X}^{-1} = \tfrac{1}{9}\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -4 \\ -4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$,
because

$$
\begin{aligned}
\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \tfrac{1}{9}\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -4 \\ -4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}
&= \tfrac{1}{9}\begin{bmatrix} 25 - 16 & -20 + 20 \\ 20 - 20 & -16 + 25 \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \matr{I}_2,
\end{aligned}
$$

and its bottom-right entry is $\tfrac{5}{9}$.
The top-right entry is $-\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{B}\matr{S}^{-1}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-\tfrac{1}{5} \cdot 4 \cdot \tfrac{5}{9}
&= -\tfrac{4}{9}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
